o1.biggest_strength: It catches the in-app checkout bug as a ship-now fix, sizes the money clearly at about 560 orders and ₹34 lakh gross margin a month, then ranks tests around the real customer doubts.
o1.biggest_mistake: A few implementation values are left as blanks or examples, and the parallel test schedule could be clearer as a factorial setup.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add the sample-size working in one short line for each test and tighten the run plan so there is no ambiguity about overlapping tests.

o2.biggest_strength: It has the strongest sample-size and profit-per-session thinking, including the right bug value, gross profit per order, post-fix baseline, and stop rules.
o2.biggest_mistake: It uses one blanket all-traffic, 4-week, 10% MDE rule for every test, which is less tailored for the mobile size-picker and hero-image tests and less directly answers the 'for each test' ask.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make the traffic split, main metric, guardrail and MDE explicit inside each test, with mobile-only reads where the evidence is mobile-specific.

reason: Both are strong and usable, but Output 1 is a little more owner-ready because each ranked test is tied directly to the evidence, metric, split, runtime and MDE, and it handles the mobile/browser split more carefully.
